response.cue_rationale: The religious-sponsor sense is clear and both answers fit it; this excludes the criminal or figurative sense of “godfather.”

preference_risk.rationale: A baptism-based form is plausibly ordinary in both varieties and may compete with the proposed national preference.

response.rationale: Both forms can denote a man serving as a child's religious sponsor, with Indonesian commonly using “bapak baptis” and Malaysian Malay using “bapa wali.” The contrast is useful but not exclusive.
response.risk_rationale: The strength and regional distribution of “bapa wali” versus the shared “bapa/bapak baptis” alternative may vary by Christian community and register.
response.shared_synonym_rationale: “Bapa/bapak baptis” may also be understood or used in Malaysian Malay, while “bapa wali” may be understood in Indonesian religious contexts, so the national preference should not be taught as exclusive.
